item.title: MiBeeNvr v0.5.0: Full ONVIF and Hardware Transcoding
item.description:
ONVIF cameras could be discovered and their stream URL retrieved — but that was just a corner of ONVIF: PTZ control, picture adjustment, and event subscription, the parts you actually use daily, were missing. And plenty of cameras output H.265 only, which browsers can’t play directly.

PTZ and picture, adjustable

  • Drive the camera with a joystick in the web UI — pan, zoom, one-tap home
  • Presets can be created, invoked, and deleted; frequent viewpoints are one tap away
  • Brightness, contrast, saturation, and sharpness adjust live on sliders, effective immediately
  • Events the camera reports (motion detection, alarms) show up in the web UI in real time

H.265 cameras play in the browser

  • Encoding is detected automatically; H.265 is transcoded to browser-playable H.264 on hardware when needed
  • Freeze-frame anti-flicker keeps the picture smooth through the transition
  • A new transcoding monitor page shows task status and performance at a glance

Steadier

  • The Xiaomi-camera disconnect churn is fixed: a full buffer drops the oldest frame instead of tearing down the whole session
  • Reconnects moved to tiered backoff with jitter — several cameras dropping at once no longer avalanche
  • A batch of fixes: first-boot Docker crash, false health alarms, a login-redirect loop

A protocol isn’t supported until all of it is.

item.title: MiBeeNvr v0.6.0: Timelapse and Transcoding
item.description:
Once recording is up and running, the disk cries first: one 1080p camera writes tens of GB a day, and 30-day retention eats most of a 1TB drive. The community reported the same thing over and over, and timelapse plus transcoding came up as the favored fixes.

Less disk

  • Timelapse: cameras whose scenes sit still most of the day need roughly 5% of the space for the same duration
  • Frames are skipped automatically while the picture stays static — idle time isn’t wasted
  • The extraction interval is configurable, and multiple cameras stagger themselves instead of spiking together

Recordings can be transcoded

  • H.264 ↔ H.265 in both directions, with historical recordings backfillable
  • Hardware encoding is auto-detected: use it when present (the Banana Pi M5 saturates H.265 hardware encoding), disable cleanly when not — the Raspberry Pi 3B is unaffected
  • Transcoding starts from the web UI, with status and progress visible

Steadier playback, easier diagnosis

  • A frozen picture is detected automatically
  • A class of H.265 playback corruption is fixed
  • Prometheus metrics and remote logging are wired in — problems get diagnosed from data instead of guesses

Keep the disk alive first.
